results.fact: Where the Thumb is relative to Flypaper Pass / Eel Glacier
results.evidence: The contradiction is real: baseFinding puts the Thumb on the crest below Flypaper Pass on the Anderson basin side (no Eel Glacier crossing), while itinerary day 2, timing, descent, descent_text and hazards cross the Eel Glacier to reach it. The only public documentation is two trip reports by one author: one sees the Thumb on the way down from Echo Col toward the Anderson Glacier basin/Honeymoon Meadows, the other calls it a fun sandstone pinnacle; a basin photo caption lists it among features visible from ~5,252 ft above the Anderson Glacier. This leans toward the baseFinding (Anderson basin side), but no second independent source fixes its position, so no patch.

Real: itinerary day 2 schedule[4] says 'fixed anchor/bollard' while descent_text and approach_variants[0].hazards say there is no fixed hardware. No external source describes the Thumb's rappel or anchors at all (only brief trip-report asides that it is a fun sandstone climb), and only two row fields oppose the itinerary, short of the 4+-field threshold for an internal fix.

results.correct_value: about 530 ft at the Dosewallips Road washout parking
results.evidence: A trip report gives the washout parking at 550 ft; a hiking field guide starts the road-walk trailhead at 520 ft; USGS 3DEP elevation at the stored pin is 530 ft. 1,600 ft is the elevation of the old Dosewallips Ranger Station ~5.5 mi further up (Mountaineers route page), not the washout parking, and 700 ft matches neither.

results.correct_value: About 17 mi each way between the washout and the tarn high camp (day 1 in = 17, day 3 out = 17); ~38 mi round trip with the 4-mile climbing day
results.evidence: NPS gives 16 mi from the road end to Anderson Pass; the Mountaineers give 1.4 + 8 + 1.2 mi ranger station to Anderson Pass, plus the ~5.5 mi road, and describe the way trail from the pass to the tarn camp near 5,100 ft as about a mile. A family trip report put the Anderson Glacier overlook at 17-18 mi from the washout. So day 1 (washout to tarn camp) and day 3 (reverse) are each ~17 mi, matching the waypoint at mile 17; 15 and 20 were inconsistent. dist_km (19.5 mi one way to the spire) is left untouched as it is a one-way figure, not clearly a different quantity.

results.correct_value: The Anderson Glacier is gone (disappeared by ~2011); only the Eel Glacier carries crevasse hazard
results.evidence: Wikipedia (citing USGS/NPS studies and NPR) says Anderson Glacier lost over 90% of its area 1927-2009 and was gone by 2011; NPS/NPCA and Olympic Park Advocates pages likewise describe it as disappeared. obj_haz[1] and seasonal_hazards.crevasses still list crevasses on the Anderson Glacier; reworded to the Eel Glacier only (whether this route crosses the Eel at all remains flagged under the location contradiction).

patches.replace: (the Eel Glacier; the old Anderson Glacier basin is now bare rock and snowfield)

patches.find: the route crosses the Anderson/Eel Glacier on approach
patches.replace: the route crosses the Eel Glacier on approach (the Anderson Glacier itself is gone)

results.fact: Total gain in itinerary totalNote vs gain_ft
results.evidence: itinerary.totalNote says about 6,200 ft of net gain/loss, while gain_ft/loss_ft are 6,400 and the itinerary days sum to 6,400 gain and 6,400 loss. No outside source states a car-to-car gain for this Thumb objective (the only trip total found, ~9,000 ft, is for a different West Peak itinerary), so no patch.
